question.text: Ms. Priya Shah is building a peer-group benchmark for Chambal Managed Futures Fund (Cat III). She notes that Cat III AIFs in India include long-short, market-neutral, global macro, multi-strategy, arbitrage, managed-futures, and event-driven funds — all pooled into the same SEBI 'Cat III' bucket. What is the MOST fundamental challenge this poses for peer-group benchmarking?

answer.text: Strategy heterogeneity — funds with fundamentally different risk profiles are pooled into a single peer group, diluting the benchmark's relevance
Self-reporting bias — Cat III funds do not report to SEBI
Cat III funds have no fee information, so returns cannot be compared
Cat III funds use Section 115UB pass-through taxation, distorting comparability

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Cat III AIFs span radically different strategies (market-neutral 2-5% vol vs long-short 15-20% vol vs macro 10-15% vol) yet are pooled into one SEBI category. The resulting peer-group benchmark (e.g., CRISIL AIF Cat III) averages across incomparable risk profiles — strategy heterogeneity is the fundamental measurement problem. This is why PPMs typically layer a strategy-specific peer (e.g., HFRI Macro) on top of the SEBI-mandated Cat III benchmark. **The Trap:** Option B is wrong — Cat III AIFs DO report to SEBI (and to benchmarking agencies). Option C is wrong — expense and fee data are reported in the PPM. Option D is wrong — Cat III is taxed at FUND LEVEL at MMR (Section 115UB does NOT apply to Cat III; it applies to Cat I/II only). **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-D (Cat I/II Manager) uses Section 115UB pass-through — that trap is specifically a Cat I/II concept being mis-applied to Cat III here. XIX-B tests the strategy-heterogeneity challenge from the distributor-disclosure perspective. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Supplement the CRISIL AIF Cat III peer benchmark with a strategy-native global peer (HFRI Macro for macro funds, HFRI Equity Market Neutral for market-neutral, HFRI Event-Driven for event-driven) in your investor letter. Let LPs see both the Indian Cat III umbrella AND your true strategy peer — sophisticated LPs already do this analysis themselves; beat them to it.
